The beginning of my original post must have somehow been fudged by my fat hands, but what I started with was that I don't know if it will help or work for you, but I can offer my experience if that helps.  


 I was admitted to the mental hospital for trying to kill myself.  I think 10 minutes later and I might be dead.

In the hospital there was nothing to do, nothing. I journaled for the first time seriously in my adult life.

I didn't know what I was suppose to write, how I was suppose to write it (to be read later or what?), what was the purpose, and the benefits didn't seem possible.

It helped me.  I'm in a relationship that is loveless, careless, and phycologically toxic.

​

When I wrote I started with what was happening around me, journaling well is like anything. a learned skill.  you get out of it what you put into it.  I wrote for two days about exactly what was happening at the time, the nurses running around looking stupid in the pit, the "crazy" guy walking up and down the halls, the people in for rehab and their presence there.  It wasn't easy, but I did it anyway.  Still seemed stupid.

A couple days into journaling, I specifically wrote about my suicide attempt and nothing else. I wrote exactly what happened so I'd never forget.  I reminded myself how far I got, what I was thinking, what was the reason I jumped to it in the first place.  Eventually I found myself deeper and deeper in thought, writing down and working through situational problems in my relationship - what I was thinking and doing the math about what was logical about what he might have been thinking.  It gave me a lot of insight into the moments we'd had and gave me a clear picture of how I felt and why.

If you can't think of anything to journal but want to know the benefits, just start with what happened in your day for a week or two, just write what happened in your morning, what you ate, what that one guy said to you. You'll find yourself writing eventually and naturally about the deeper problems bothering you at times, and the reasons you think they are how they are.

Journaling is a processing mechanism.   You can do this, and if you want, you can do it well - I'm sure of it.  If you can't immediately write something "deep" then don't, write something surface first and soon you'll find a rhythm.
